widget_vocab.icon_multi: tap device/channel/category icons; each shows a small rendered sample
widget_vocab.icon_pick: tap one icon from a small set
widget_vocab.style_board: board of labelled app-style screenshots; tap to like or avoid (credit the shown apps on the tile)
widget_vocab.chip_select: tap word chips from a curated vocabulary; free-type to add
widget_vocab.visual_abc: 2-4 rendered mockups of the same thing; tap the one you mean
widget_vocab.brand_kit: logo upload + colour picker with a live header preview
widget_vocab.screen_picker: tap a screen thumbnail per role
widget_vocab.screen_map: map of all screens; tap a lock to make one public/private
widget_vocab.drag_order: drag items to reorder a live preview (menu, columns)
widget_vocab.card_board: editable cards per inventory list; tap to remove, type to add
widget_vocab.form_builder: live form preview that rebuilds as fields are added/typed/reordered; conditional fields toggle live
widget_vocab.tap_on_preview: answer by tapping the element on a rendered mockup (title field, lock stage, button placement)
widget_vocab.access_matrix: roles x verbs grid with per-cell scope; renders a see-it-as-that-role sample underneath
widget_vocab.pipeline_editor: stages as draggable pills; draw arrows for moves; badges for approval/timeout; tap an arrow to set who moves it
widget_vocab.link_diagram: record cards on a canvas; drag a line between two to declare the relationship
widget_vocab.login_preview: live sign-in screen; toggling a method adds/removes its button
widget_vocab.message_preview: rendered sample message per channel (email/SMS bubble/push banner); edit intent under it
widget_vocab.report_mockup: rendered report with toggleable filter chips and a date-range control
widget_vocab.pricing_builder: plan cards edited in place on a live pricing-page preview
widget_vocab.wireframe_walkthrough: clickable wireframe of every screen; every numbered button present; tap through and confirm

parts.title: Setup
parts.intro: Asked once. Changes how much the interviewer asks, never what gets built or verified.

parts.title: The idea
parts.intro: Conversational. The interviewer may ask these in any words; the script decides when each field is filled.

parts.title: Permissions — roles
parts.intro: Once per confirmed role, except the super role from A.16. Authority over specific things is asked where it is exercised (Records, Flow, Billing).

parts.title: Flow — processes and external systems
parts.intro: Once per confirmed workflow, including every record lifecycle from R.10. Integrations are Flow instances (FL.X questions).

parts.title: Flow — external systems
parts.intro: Once per confirmed external system (incl. 'Public API' if A.11 = yes).

parts.title: Notify
parts.intro: Once per confirmed notification, including those created by FL.11 and RP.08 (those arrive pre-filled and only ask what is still empty).

parts.title: Read-back
parts.intro: Generated by the script from earlier answers. The owner confirms or corrects; nothing new is asked.

questions.prompt: How involved do you want to be? Full (you decide everything), guided (you decide the product things, I'll propose the rest and you confirm), or hands-off (you answer the essentials, I'll fill the rest with standard behaviour and show you the list at the end).
questions.notes: Sets how many derived/defaulted values are read back for confirmation. Never changes the spec's content.

questions.prompt: What are you trying to build? Describe it like you're explaining it to a friend.
questions.notes: Done only when at least one record noun can be extracted. Feeds the A.15 inventory proposal.

questions.prompt: What should people be able to accomplish with it?
Who is it for?
How will you know it's working — what does success look like to you?
What is the app called?
questions.notes: Dropped in the handoff's final pass. It appears on every screen and email; two builders would invent two names.

questions.prompt: Where will people use it — in a web browser, as a phone app (iOS/Android), both, or as a desktop program?
questions.notes: Never asked in the handoff. The single biggest divergence between two builders.

questions.prompt: Do people need to log in / have accounts?
Is this for one organisation/user base, or for many separate organisations that must never see each other's data?
Does this involve charging people money?
Which parts, if any, can be seen without logging in? (e.g. a public landing page, a public booking form, nothing)
questions.notes: 'Nothing' is a valid answer and must be recorded explicitly.

questions.prompt: Do other systems need to push data into, or pull data out of, your app automatically (an API, webhooks)?
Is there existing data that has to be brought in before launch (a spreadsheet, an old system)? If so, what and where from?
What country are most of your users in, and do you need more than one language?
questions.notes: Drives date/number/currency display format and default timezone. Never asked in the handoff.

questions.prompt: Is there anything you want to work differently from how a typical app of this kind normally works?
Here's what I understood you'll need — screens, records, roles, forms, notifications, file types, reports, workflows, external systems. Did I miss anything, or get anything wrong? (confirm each list)
questions.notes: Engine proposes from A.01–A.04; owner corrects. Each confirmed item instantiates its part. Empty lists are allowed but must be confirmed empty.

questions.prompt: Is there one role that can always do everything, no matter what? If so, which one?
questions.notes: That role is skipped in every per-record/per-workflow authority question and granted everything. Removes dozens of repeat answers.

questions.prompt: Are there other apps, brands or products whose look and feel you want this to resemble — or specifically avoid?
In three words, how should this feel to use? (e.g. playful, fast, minimal / serious, trustworthy, dense)
How much should be visible at once — spacious and simple, balanced, or dense and information-rich?
Is there a primary colour, logo or existing brand material to build from? If not, pick a mark from the starter library (packages/builder/assets/logos/manifest.json) or leave it to be designed later.
questions.notes: 'premade' exists so an app never ships with a blank or broken logo slot while a real one is pending -- the customer picks a real, named starter mark rather than the app defaulting to nothing. 'provided' is validated against the starter library's own manifest.spec (format, aspect ratio, size, background) by the Builder, which refuses a file that doesn't meet it rather than resizing or reinterpreting it.

questions.prompt: On phones, should it be a simplified version of the big-screen layout, or does anything need to work completely differently on mobile?
questions.notes: Only asked if there is a big-screen platform to simplify from.

questions.prompt: After logging in, which screen does each role land on first?
questions.notes: Handoff classed 'what happens after login' as a system default. It is product-specific: dashboard vs list vs record. Two builders diverge.

questions.prompt: Here is the main menu I'd build from your screens, in this order: [derived]. Reorder, rename or hide anything?
How do people get an account — sign up themselves publicly, get invited by someone, or get created by an admin? (any that apply)
What information do you need from someone when they register? (each item: what it is, and is it required)
Must they verify their email address before they can use the app?
Which login methods? (any that apply)
When someone signs up by themselves, which role do they get?
questions.notes: Never asked in the handoff. Without it one builder makes new signups Members, another makes them Admins.

questions.prompt: Who can invite people, and which role does an invited person get by default?
Is two-factor authentication required — for nobody, admins only, or everyone? And by which method — authenticator app, SMS code, or either?
questions.notes: Handoff's classification said MFA method stays a closed question; the final interview lost it.

questions.prompt: After how many failed login attempts should an account be temporarily locked, and for how long? ('never lock' is a valid answer)
Can one person be logged in on more than one device at the same time?
How long can someone stay signed in before being asked to sign in again?
Can accounts be suspended? If so, who can do it, and does anything trigger it automatically (e.g. unpaid bill)?
Can accounts be deleted? By whom — the person themselves, an admin, or both? And what happens to their data: kept, anonymised, or fully erased?
Who, if anyone, may reset someone else's password on their behalf?
Must people accept terms of service / a privacy policy when they sign up? Do those documents exist already?
Can one person hold more than one role at the same time?
questions.notes: Asked once, not per role. Decides single-select vs multi-select role assignment — a visible difference.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, who is a '${role}' — what kind of person holds this role?
questions.notes: Context only. Never a build-spec source by itself.

questions.prompt: Can a '${role}' see other people's private information anywhere in the app (personal settings, contact details, private notes)?
Can a '${role}' see or change billing and payment details?
Who can give someone the '${role}' role, or take it away?
What does a '${record}' represent, in one sentence?
What information does a '${record}' store? For each item: what kind is it, is it required, must it be unique, and (for a list choice) what are the options / (for a link) which record does it link to?
questions.notes: Handoff never asked for choice options, uniqueness, or the link target. Each one makes two builders diverge.

questions.prompt: Which of those fields is the '${record}'s name — the thing shown in lists, links and messages?
Does a '${record}' need a human-readable number or code (like INV-0001)? If so, what format?
Who can VIEW a '${record}'? For each role: all of them, only their own, only ones linked to something they belong to (say what), or public (no login)?
questions.notes: The handoff's audit resolved the Manager example with a 'their team' scope, then the interview only offered all/own. 'linked' restores it and must name the relation.

questions.prompt: Who can CREATE a '${record}'?
Who can EDIT a '${record}'? For each role: any, only their own, or only linked ones?
Who can DELETE a '${record}'? For each role: any, only their own, or only linked ones? ('nobody' is valid)
What makes a '${record}' someone's OWN — the person who created it, or the person named in a particular field (which one)?
questions.notes: Never asked in the handoff. created_by vs assigned_to is the classic two-builder split.

questions.prompt: Does a '${record}' move through stages over its life (e.g. Draft → Active → Archived)? If so, name them in order.
Is a '${record}' connected to any other record? For each: which record, is it one-to-many or many-to-many, and must the link always exist?
When a '${record}' is deleted, what happens to the things connected to it — deleted too, kept but unlinked, or deletion blocked until they're dealt with?
Should old or inactive '${record}'s be archivable (hidden but kept) rather than deleted?
How long should '${record}' data be kept before it is permanently removed — forever, or a set time after it's archived/closed?

Besides create/edit/delete and moving through stages, are there any other buttons people need on a '${record}' (e.g. duplicate, send, print, mark as paid)? For each: who can press it, what it does, and where the result shows up.
questions.notes: This is where every non-CRUD button gets its number. Handoff derived all actions from CRUD + transitions, so 'Duplicate' could never exist.

questions.prompt: What is the '${form}' for, and who fills it out?
Which record does it create or edit? And does it collect anything that is NOT stored on that record? (list those extra items with their kind)
Does any field only appear depending on another answer? (which field, depends on which answer)
questions.notes: Handoff classified this as 'asked only if the owner indicates' but had no prompt that could surface it.

questions.prompt: Can someone save it as a draft and finish later?
Right after a successful submit, where should they end up?
What is a '${file_type}' used for, and which record is it attached to?
One per record, or many?
Who can upload it, and who can view/download it? ('public' allowed for viewing)
What kind of file — image, document, spreadsheet, video/audio, or something else (say which formats)?
Roughly how large might these get? (e.g. 10 MB, 500 MB)
If someone uploads a new version, keep the old one (history) or replace it?
When the record it belongs to is deleted, delete the file too?
What starts '${workflow}' — a person doing something (who, doing what), something happening automatically (what), or a schedule (when)?
What are its stages, in order? Which is the starting stage, and which stage(s) mean it's finished?
For each move from one stage to the next: is it done by a person (which roles) or does it happen automatically when something happens (what)?
questions.notes: Handoff only allowed a person as mover. 'Order becomes Paid when payment arrives' had no home.

questions.prompt: Must anything be true before a move is allowed (e.g. can't ship without an address)? For each move: the condition, or none.
Does any stage need someone's approval before it can move on? Which stage, and which roles approve?
If an approver says no, which stage does it go back to, and can it be resubmitted?
questions.notes: Handoff locked 'standard advance/revert' as a default. Back to previous vs back to start vs terminal Rejected are three different products.

questions.prompt: Can it be cancelled? By whom, and from which stages?
Once it reaches a finished stage, what should happen? (e.g. nothing, lock it, send something, create something)
From which stage onward, if any, should the record become read-only?
Does any stage have a time limit? Which stage, how long, and what happens when it runs out?
Should anyone be told when it moves stage? Which moves, who, and by which channel?
questions.notes: Owners never list 'tell the assignee on stage change' as a notification in A.15. Asked here so it exists.

questions.prompt: Why do you need '${integration}' — what is it for?
What does your app send to it, and what does it get back?
When does that exchange happen — when something happens in your app (what), on a schedule (when), or when someone presses a button (who)?
Is it one connection for the whole organisation, or does each person connect their own account?
If '${integration}' is unavailable, what should the person see — a blocking message, nothing (it quietly retries later), or the app carries on without it?
What sends '${notification}' — something happening (what), a time relative to a date on a record (which date, how long before/after), or a fixed schedule?
Who receives it — roles, the record's owner, a person named in a field on the record (which), or someone else?
Which channels — email, SMS, push, in-app? (any)
What should the recipient understand or do after reading it? (exact wording is drafted at build time and sent to you to approve)
Can the recipient switch this one off?
What question does '${report}' answer for the person reading it?
Who can view it?
Is it a live screen in the app, a downloadable document, or both? And shown as a table, a chart, or both?
What numbers/metrics does it show? (list them)
For '${metric}': exactly how is it calculated — when does something count, and as at which date?
questions.notes: Fires once per metric whose name contains a flagged term. Unanswered = build blocked, never defaulted.

questions.prompt: What should it be filterable or grouped by, and what date range should it show by default?
Can it be exported? By whom?
Should it be sent to anyone automatically on a schedule? Who, how often?
What are you charging for — subscriptions, one-off purchases, usage, or a mix?
Who pays — each person, or a whole organisation at once?
List your plans. For each: name, price, how often it's billed, what's included, and any limits. Is there a free plan?
What currency do you bill in?
Is there a free trial? How long, and is a card required to start it?
questions.notes: Never asked in the handoff.

questions.prompt: What unit is counted for usage billing, and when is it charged?
Card only, or can customers also pay by invoice / bank transfer?
questions.notes: Locked as 'card via gateway' in the handoff. Pay-by-invoice changes the product (manual reconciliation, dunning), so it is asked.

questions.prompt: If a payment fails: keep access for how many days before restricting? And after repeated failure — suspend, downgrade to free, or cancel?
Can customers change plan themselves? Does an upgrade take effect immediately or at the next cycle? A downgrade?
Can customers cancel themselves? Do they keep access until the end of the paid period, or lose it immediately?
Are refunds allowed? Who exactly may issue one?
Can one person belong to more than one organisation?
How does a new organisation come to exist — someone signs up and creates it, or you (the operator) create it?
Inside an organisation, which role manages its members and settings?
questions.notes: Never asked in the handoff. Without it, no builder knows who invites people into an org.

questions.prompt: Are the roles the same in every organisation, or can each organisation define its own?
Is there an operator role (you) that can see across all organisations? Which role?
By default, is everything about an organisation — records, files, reports, billing, workflows — completely separate from the others? If not, what is shared and how?
Can organisations set their own branding (logo, colours)?
Can an organisation be suspended or deleted? By whom, and what happens to its members and data?

You said '${deviation}' should work differently from the standard. Which standard behaviour is it replacing, exactly what should happen instead, and which screens/records does it apply to? Everything you don't mention keeps the standard behaviour.

Here is everything the app will do on its own, with nobody clicking: [derived list of scheduled jobs — retention purges, stage time-outs, date-relative reminders, scheduled reports, subscription renewals, trial expiries, integration syncs]. Correct?
questions.notes: This is the recurring-ops namespace. Each item gets its own OPS-nnn id.

questions.prompt: Here is every numbered button/action in the app and where its result lands: [derived]. Correct?
Here is every screen, who can open it, and what it shows: [derived]. Correct?

system_defaults.behaviour: Secrets in an environment vault, never in code or the database.
AES-256 at rest for database and file storage.
TLS everywhere; HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite cookies.
UUIDv4 primary keys on every table.
created_at/updated_at/created_by/updated_by on every table.
15 s request timeout → transaction aborted, HTTP 504.
Failed external calls retry 3× with exponential backoff + jitter.
Payment webhooks signature-verified and processed exactly once.
Submit buttons disable on click.
RFC 7807 error bodies; stack traces masked in production.
Structured JSON audit log of every mutation and failed authorisation.
Private object storage for uploads.
Async malware scan before a file is marked active.
Failed upload/scan → file marked broken, transaction rolled back, 400.
Row-level security enforces organisation isolation in the database.
Nightly encrypted backups, 30-day retention.
Signed session tokens; CSRF-safe cookie rules.
Every notification logged with channel, recipient, status, retries.
3 delivery retries then dead-letter.
Generated documents stored transiently behind 1-hour signed URLs.
Report generation times out at 60 s.
One fixed REST convention for every endpoint, verb and envelope.
Standard loading / empty / error / success / back / leave-and-return behaviour on every screen.
Each field type carries one standard validation rule and error message.
Reports regenerate on demand, cached 5 min.
Tax computed by the payment gateway from the billing address.
Message wording drafted at build time and approved by the owner before launch; never shipped unseen.
Allowed formats come from a fixed allow-list per file category.
Every node's pass/fail check is generated from that node's own answers.
The email address is the account identity; changing it requires re-verification.
system_defaults.why: Handoff never stated what identifies an account.

system_defaults.behaviour: Self-service reset by emailed link, valid 1 hour.
One-time recovery codes issued at MFA enrolment.
system_defaults.why: Classification kept this as a question; owners cannot meaningfully choose otherwise.

system_defaults.behaviour: Every user can edit their own name, email, password and notification preferences.
A suspended user sees a fixed 'account suspended — contact <support contact>' screen and nothing else.
The first super-role account is seeded from the deploy inputs, not created through the app.
system_defaults.why: A complete working app needs a first login; nothing in the handoff created one.

system_defaults.behaviour: Light theme only; WCAG 2.1 AA contrast and keyboard access.
Dates, numbers and currency display in the format of A.13's region; stored in UTC; shown in the viewer's timezone.
Last save wins; a user saving over a newer version is warned and shown the newer version.
Every record list is searchable and filterable on its visible fields, sorted newest first, exportable by anyone who can view it.
A failed submit shows inline errors and keeps what was typed; forms are single-page; public forms get spam protection.
If any notification uses in-app, the app has one notification inbox with read/unread state.
Images get thumbnails; downloads are served by signed URL.
Hitting a plan limit shows an upgrade prompt, then blocks the action.
Card, billing address and tax IDs are collected by the gateway's hosted form; invoices/receipts are the gateway's.
Mid-cycle plan changes are prorated by the gateway.
A person in several organisations switches with a standard switcher; each organisation has its own timezone setting defaulting to A.13.
Invitations expire after 7 days and can be re-sent.

derivations.rule: Fixed 1:1 map from field type to column type.
Form fields = target record's fields + extra fields.
A screen shows its record/form fields; a role sees a screen if it can view/act on anything on it.
Permitted = every explicit grant; forbidden = everything else (default deny); admin = any user-management grant.
Immediate on event; offset for relative_to_date; cron for schedule.
derivations.safe_because: Read from the owner's own trigger.

derivations.rule: File inherits its parent record's retention.
Unflagged metric = count/sum of the named field; flagged metric = RP.05 text.
Edges exactly as listed in FL.03; nothing added.
Operator role sees all orgs; everyone else sees their memberships.
Each subscription event links to one plan by name.
Every duration/schedule answer becomes one OPS-nnn job; confirmed in Z.01.
derivations.safe_because: Mechanical collection; owner confirms the list.

derivations.rule: One numbered action per create/edit/delete grant, custom action, transition, cancel, approve, and form submit.
One list + one detail screen per record, one per form/report, plus landing per role.
derivations.safe_because: Enumeration; owner confirms in Z.03 / C.07.

derivations.rule: Choice options become an enum with the exact listed values.
For every numbered action and transition: perform it as each role, assert the declared outcome and location.
derivations.safe_because: Definitionally downstream of answers; no LLM in the pass/fail path.

deploy_inputs.prompt: Web address (domain) the app will live at
Sender name and email address for outgoing email
Support contact shown to users (email or URL)
Email address of the first super-role account
SMS provider credentials and sender ID
OAuth client credentials for each social login chosen
Credentials / API keys for each external system
Terms of service and privacy policy documents (or a request to draft them)
